newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. and Iraq agree on arms inspection plan - INA.
newsitem.headline: U.N. and Iraq agree on arms inspection plan - INA.

text.p: United Nations arms envoy Richard Butler has agreed with Iraqi officials on a plan to eradicate Iraq's remaining weapons of mass destruction, the Iraqi News Agency INA said on Friday.
INA said Butler, chairman of the United Nations Special Commission (UNSCOM) on Iraq, told reporters before leaving Baghdad on Friday he was determined to end his mission as quickly as possible.
"Butler stressed that during talks with Iraqi officials a working plan was drawn up to specify tasks and achieve the remaining...issues (between Iraq and UNSCOM)," it said.

The agency said Butler conducted several meetings with Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz, Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed and head of the Iraqi Military Industrialisation Commission, Abdultawab Mulahwaish, since his arrival on Monday.

Butler took over from Sweden's Rolf Ekeus who led UNSCOM, the United Nations body entrusted with dismantling Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, since its inception soon after the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations can lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, although Baghdad is allowed limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
"We did design some work tasks in each of the areas for the month ahead. They must be completed in that time and they should have concrete and practical results.
"...There is a determination to get this work done," Butler said.
He said he would come back to Iraq in a month or so to check if that plan was implemented and to set up further work tasks with the Iraqis.
Butler said he would submit a report to the U.N. Security Council by October 11 this year, the time when the council will review its trade sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"I have promised (Iraq's) Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz that the commission will report objectively and fully on the state of progress...," he added.

Last month Iraq barred U.N. inspectors from entering three sensitive sites, prompting the Security Council to issue a resolution warning Iraq it would face further sanctions if it blocked U.N. inspectors.
